candidates.summary: objectInfo is priced flat (Base 1200, SizeFlat) but declaredTypeName builds dt.PkgPath + "." + dt.Name on every call, so its cost scales with a type name the caller declares, bounded only by MaxTxBytes; the row comment and the bench header both claim nothing scales with caller input
candidates.failure_scenario: A realm declares `type <60000 x A> struct{}` and `var p = &<name>{}`, then loops reflect.Of(p). Per iteration gas goes 12,495 -> 22,235 (the rise is allocation gas for the returned string only) while wall time goes 9.1-16.5 us -> 50.4-79.7 us: ~0.7-1.3 ns/gas against ~2.3-3.6 ns/gas, the marginal bytes near 6 ns/gas. On chain the name can reach ~490 KB (two occurrences in a 1 MB tx), where the per-byte part dominates, so a block of these calls runs several times longer than its gas says.
